description: Add persistent scoreboard (name entry on game over, top-10 leaderboard, mid-game peek) and Nuitka build support (pyproject.toml, Makefile with Linux+macOS targets).

userStories.title: Create score persistence module
userStories.description: As a developer, I need pure functions to load and save scores to disk so that game results persist across sessions without coupling persistence logic to the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Create yahtzee/scores.py with three functions: load_scores(), save_score(name, score), get_top_10()

load_scores() reads ~/.local/share/yahtzee/scores.json and returns a list of dicts [{name, score, date}]; returns [] if file missing or JSON is malformed (silently resets on error, prints warning to stderr)

save_score(name: str, score: int) appends a new entry to the list with today's date (stdlib datetime, YYYY-MM-DD format) and writes the full list back; creates the directory and file if they don't exist
get_top_10() returns the top 10 entries from load_scores() sorted by score descending
Scores file format: {"scores": [{"name": "...", "score": 0, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}, ...]}
All file I/O uses pathlib.Path and json from stdlib only — no third-party libraries
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Create ScoreboardScreen modal
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see the top 10 scores in a ranked table so that I know where I stand after a game or mid-game.
acceptanceCriteria: Create yahtzee/scoreboard_screen.py with ScoreboardScreen(ModalScreen)
ScoreboardScreen accepts a mode parameter: 'postgame' (shows N/Q hints) or 'peek' (shows 'any key to close' hint)
Displays top-10 scores from get_top_10() in a fixed-width ASCII table with columns: Rank, Name, Score, Date — aligned with box-drawing characters (┌─┬─┐ style) or plain ASCII pipes and dashes
If fewer than 10 scores exist, only the rows that exist are shown (no placeholder rows)
If no scores exist, shows a centered 'No scores yet!' message instead of a table
In 'postgame' mode: pressing Enter or N starts a new game (dismiss with 'new_game'); pressing Q quits (dismiss with 'quit')
In 'peek' mode: any key dismisses the modal (dismiss with None) and returns to the game with no state change
Modal uses dark theme consistent with existing modals: #16213e background, #f0883e accent border, #8b949e hint text
Keyboard-only; no mouse handlers
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Create NameEntryScreen modal
userStories.description: As a player, I want to type my name after a game ends so it is saved alongside my score.
acceptanceCriteria: Create yahtzee/name_entry_screen.py with NameEntryScreen(ModalScreen)
Modal shows a title 'Game Over — Enter your name' and a Textual Input widget (max_length=20)
Pressing Enter submits the name; if the input is empty, the name defaults to 'Anonymous'
On submit, dismiss(name_string) is called so the caller receives the entered name
Modal uses dark theme consistent with existing modals: #16213e background, #f0883e accent border, #8b949e hint text
Input widget has focus on mount so the player can type immediately without pressing Tab
Keyboard-only; no mouse handlers
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Wire post-game flow: name entry → save → scoreboard
userStories.description: As a player, I want the name entry and scoreboard screens to appear automatically after the game-over screen so my score is saved and I see the leaderboard without extra steps.
acceptanceCriteria: In yahtzee/app.py, update _handle_game_over() so that after the game-over screen is dismissed (result == 'new_game' or 'quit'), a NameEntryScreen is pushed first
The NameEntryScreen callback receives the entered name, calls save_score(name, self.game.grand_total) from yahtzee/scores.py, then pushes ScoreboardScreen(mode='postgame')
The ScoreboardScreen 'postgame' callback: if result == 'new_game' → call _reset_game(); if result == 'quit' → call self.exit()
The existing game-over screen (game_over_screen.py) is NOT modified — the new screens are chained after it
The flow order is: GameOverScreen → NameEntryScreen → ScoreboardScreen
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add S keybinding for mid-game scoreboard peek
userStories.description: As a player, I want to press S at any point during a game to see the current leaderboard so I know what score I'm aiming for without ending my turn.
acceptanceCriteria: Add ('s', 'show_scoreboard', 'Scores') to YahtzeeApp.BINDINGS
action_show_scoreboard() pushes ScoreboardScreen(mode='peek')
Any key dismisses the peek modal and returns to the game with all state (dice, held, roll_count, scores) unchanged
The S binding appears in the Textual footer alongside R, N, Q
If no scores have been saved yet, the modal shows 'No scores yet!' (handled by ScoreboardScreen from US-002)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add pyproject.toml and expose run() entry point
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a pyproject.toml so the package is pip-installable and its console script entry point is declared for Nuitka and end users.
acceptanceCriteria: Create pyproject.toml at the project root with [project] section: name='yahtzee', version='1.0.0', description='Single-player Yahtzee TUI', requires-python='>=3.10', dependencies=['textual>=0.60']
[project.scripts] declares: yahtzee = 'yahtzee.__main__:run'
yahtzee/__main__.py exposes def run(): YahtzeeApp().run() (in addition to the existing if __name__ == '__main__': block)
Running python -m yahtzee from the project root still launches the app
Running yahtzee after pip install -e . launches the app
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add Makefile with Nuitka build targets
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a make build command that compiles the app into a self-contained single-file binary so users can run Yahtzee without installing Python.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Makefile at the project root
build-linux target runs: python -m nuitka --onefile --output-filename=yahtzee --enable-plugin=no-qt --include-data-dir=yahtzee:yahtzee yahtzee/__main__.py
build-macos target runs the same command (identical flags; Nuitka handles platform differences automatically)
build target detects the current OS using uname and delegates to build-linux or build-macos accordingly
clean target removes: yahtzee.bin yahtzee.build/ yahtzee.dist/ yahtzee.onefile-build/ and the output binary named yahtzee
Makefile includes .PHONY declarations for build, build-linux, build-macos, clean
Typecheck passes
